idee_recherchee.texte: Time passes more slowly for an astronaut orbiting Earth or for a clock near a massive object than for someone far from gravity, an effect called time dilation that has been measured with atomic clocks and must be corrected in GPS satellites.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Dilatation du temps : ce que voit un observateur extérieur
resume: For someone watching from far away, time seems to slow as you approach the event horizon and you appear to stop moving there, remaining alive nearly forever before eventually disappearing. This follows Einstein's relativity, where more gravity slows time, so a falling person is spaghettified, frozen in time and destroyed depending on the viewpoint.
texte: However, things get even stranger for someone who is watching you fall into a black hole from far away. As you approach [music] the event horizon and gravity increases, time seems to slow down. To the observer, you would seem to be moving so slowly that [music] it'd be hard for them to tell if you were moving at all. In fact, once you hit the event horizon, you would seem to [music] stop moving completely. This means that to an outside observer, you would be alive just before the event horizon practically forever because it would take many of their lifetimes before your body would pass beyond that point and disappear into the singularity of the black hole. Eventually, you would just disappear from the observer's perspective, [music] but it'd take a very, very long time. This all has to do with the perspective and what Albert Einstein called relativity. [music] Basically, the more gravity there is, the slower time moves for you than someone [music] who's observing you where there's less gravity. So, if you were to fall into a black hole, you would be spaghettified, [music] frozen in time, and destroyed all at once, depending on what perspective you were viewing the interaction from. Needless to say, things get really weird the closer you get to a black hole.
